Batterie.et: In the military sense (early 17th c.) from French batterie. The electronic sense (late 18th c.) is a semantic loan from English battery.

Bataillon.et: Borrowed from French bataillon, from Italian battaglione.

s: a surname, Battenberg, transferred from the place name, equivalent to English Mountbatten
Battenberg.et: Inherited from Old High German Bettenberg, from Batto, a personal name from Proto-West Germanic *badu (“battle”) + berg (“mountain, hill”). The surname derives from the town in Hesse.

b: Da schien der Mond ganz helle, und die weißen Kieselsteine, die vor dem Haus lagen, glänzten wie lauter Batzen.
